clue.text: Onion that's plausibly gold and bronze?

explanation.surface: A question about whether an onion could pass for gold and bronze.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as SILVER'S KIN: gold and bronze are fellow medal metals, so they could plausibly be counted as relatives of silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A small white pickling onion is a variety called by this name; and gold and bronze are relatives of silver among Olympic medal metals.

clue.text: Indication new US soldiers will be turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the pieces are read upwards, from bottom to top, so they come out backwards

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers, so the plural gives GIS

explanation.surface: A hint that freshly arrived American troops are about to appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be turning up' reverses N + GIS, giving SIGN, read upwards as in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is a token or signal that points to something, so it serves as an indication.

clue.text: Lapse getting 'S' misplaced?

parts.note: a slip of the tongue in which the sound of the letter S comes out wrong, said as a soft th

explanation.surface: Asks whether a mistake comes from putting the letter S in the wrong place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misplaced' suggests an anagram or a moved letter, but no letters are shuffled: the clue describes a speech defect in which S is mispronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: This speech impediment turns a sibilant into a th sound, so it is a lapse in saying the letter S.

clue.text: Rages with remorse, possibly providing explanation of mistake

indicators.note: possibly says the letters given may form something else, so they are to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a fury full of remorse, perhaps explaining an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the twelve letters of RAGES and REMORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer prints a notice like this to tell the user what went wrong and why.

clue.text: Passage offered by head of state in America

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of state is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A route offered by a governor of an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' looks like a corridor or a piece of text; here it is a cavity in the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an air-filled cavity or channel in the bones of the face, so a passage in anatomy.

clue.text: "I'm a mess about fashion' — and even that's saying too much!

indicators.note: about means the outer pieces wrap round the inner one

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
a sty is a filthy place, a mess
mode is a fashion or style

explanation.surface: Someone moans that they look a fright about their clothes, and then admits even that remark is boasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the fashion word with the other two pieces. The definition is playful: even calling yourself a mess talks about yourself, and that is saying too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of modesty shows in boastful talk, saying more about oneself than is seemly.

clue.text: Nothing the matter in work

parts.note: O is the round zero, nothing
pus is the matter that forms in an infected wound

explanation.surface: A zero issue in someone's job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the matter' reads as 'what's wrong', but it is the discharge from a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Composers number each musical work as an opus.

clue.text: I came down in political group, showing preference

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the political group

parts.note: a party is a political group
alit means landed or came down, past tense of alight

explanation.surface: A newcomer descends among a political faction and reveals bias.
explanation.definitionFit: Partiality is a liking or bias for one thing over others, so a preference.

clue.text: Sulphur spoils mineral leading to suffering after long journey

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
addles means spoils or makes rotten, as with an egg
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: A chemist notes sulphur ruining a rock specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider who has spent long hours on horseback ends up chafed and aching, which is this condition.

clue.text: Government's foremost science — the study of restaurants!

indicators.note: the foremost letter of a word is its first, so only the start of Government's is used

parts.note: astronomy is the science of the stars

explanation.surface: A ministry's leading discipline turns out to be researching where to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on stars: restaurants are rated in stars, so their study sits beside the science of stars.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the art and study of good eating, which is what restaurant critics practise.

clue.text: Good free network

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear

explanation.surface: A fine free system of connections.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a lattice of crossing lines, such as the national electricity network.

clue.text: Prevent one involved in old Peruvian treaty getting worried

parts.note: the Incas were the ancient people of Peru

indicators.note: involved in means the one letter is enclosed within the treaty

parts.note: a pact is a treaty
I is the Roman numeral one
ate is worried, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: Something stops a man caught up in an ancient Peruvian agreement from fretting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' puts the one inside the treaty. Worried here is the sense of eat meaning trouble, as in 'what's eating you?'; 'Prevent' means disable someone from acting.
explanation.definitionFit: To disable someone stops them acting, so it is to prevent them.

clue.text: Leader's power's associated with home base

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power, as in physics
residential describes things to do with where people live

explanation.surface: A chief's authority is tied to their home base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader's' is a possessive standing for an adjective: belonging to a president, the leader of a republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something belonging to a president, the elected head of a state, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Reduced representation — with something fishy about it?

explanation.surface: A miniature copy that seems somehow suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading makes the phrase a model covered in scales, like a fish; 'fishy' means suspicious on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniature replica built in proportion to the real thing is a reduced representation; read differently, it is a figure covered in fish scales.

clue.text: Small-scale performance has no women dancing

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about, so these are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A modest stage show with no female dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges HAS NO WOMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo show staged by a single performer is a small-scale production.

clue.text: National survey includes working with society to get agreement

indicators.note: includes means the survey holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a census is a national count of the population
on means working, as in a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A nationwide poll that covers jobs and community finds everyone in accord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' places the working and society pieces just after the survey's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A general accord reached by a whole group is a shared agreement.

clue.text: Recorder mangling Ron's piano

indicators.note: mangling means the letters are crushed and twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recording device ruins someone's piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recorder' suggests a tape machine; it is a small woodwind instrument. 'mangling' rearranges RONS PIANO.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the smallest, highest member of the recorder family of wind instruments.

clue.text: Shortly live with the French-here?

indicators.note: shortly means a word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: are is a form of 'be', meaning live or exist
les is French for 'the' before a plural

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a brief stay among the French should be in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' cuts ARE to AR. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a place where one would live with the French.
explanation.definitionFit: This town in Provence is somewhere in France, where one would live among French people.

clue.text: head of maggot in fruit

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'head of maggot in fruit' starts lower case and is cut short: LIMES is M in LIES, but no word for LIES remains, and no scan or search gives the missing start.

clue.text: Normal situation involves steamy misbehaving for government official

indicators.note: involves means the normal situation wraps round the other letters

parts.note: par is the normal state, as in 'on a par'

indicators.note: misbehaving means the letters behave badly and fall out of order

explanation.surface: An ordinary state of affairs turns to steamy misconduct for a civil servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' rearranges the steamy letters into AYMASTE, and 'involves' sets that within the normal-situation word. The Paymaster General is a UK government post.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paymaster General is a British minister, and the title names an official who disburses wages.

clue.text: Note marriage's not right when arranged as this!

definitions.text: Note marriage's not right when arranged as this!

indicators.note: not says a piece is taken away before the rearranging
when arranged means the remaining letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe giving an S

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a marriage goes wrong when it is set up as a threesome.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one R from NOTE MARRIAGES and rearrange the rest. The whole clue is also the definition: a three-way relationship is a marriage that is 'not right'.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase names a household of three lovers, which is an unconventional arrangement for a couple.

clue.text: City presumably offering a reliable bargain?

explanation.surface: Asks whether a town is likely to give shoppers a fair deal.
explanation.walkthrough: RIPON is a cathedral city in North Yorkshire. The second reading treats it as the opposite of a rip-off: a deal that is 'on', not 'off'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripon is an English cathedral city; and a deal that is the reverse of a swindle would be a bargain you can trust.

clue.text: Learner's taken in small amount-there's a shock

indicators.note: taken in means the learner is enclosed by the small amount

parts.note: a jot is a tiny amount
L is the learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A learner takes only a little of something and is startled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' puts L inside JOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden jerk or a nasty surprise is a jolt, a physical or emotional shock.

clue.text: Scots girl one's linked to US city

parts.note: I is one, and 's stands for 'is', giving I and S
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A Scottish lass is connected to an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Isla is a girl's name common in Scotland.

clue.text: Writer tricked regressive lecturer

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the tricking word is read in reverse

parts.note: to be had is to be tricked or fooled

explanation.surface: An author fooled a lecturer who has gone backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regressive' reverses HAD to DAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl was a British author of children's books and short stories.

clue.text: Pellucid piano had us in a daze?

indicators.note: a mind in a daze is muddled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clear-toned piano left the listeners stunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a daze' rearranges PIANO HAD US.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something so thin and clear that light passes through it, as with fine fabric.

clue.text: Regulation applied to new area of grass

parts.note: a law is a regulation

explanation.surface: A rule is applied to a newly sown patch of turf.
explanation.definitionFit: A mown stretch of turf in a garden or park is this.

clue.text: Flower arrangement, in conclusion, I initially admired

indicators.note: in places the arrangement inside the conclusion

parts.note: a point is the conclusion of an argument, what it comes to
a set is an arrangement, as of hair or a stage

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of admired is used

explanation.surface: Someone first admired a floral arrangement at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the arrangement inside the conclusion. 'Flower arrangement' looks like one phrase; the definition is only 'Flower', and 'arrangement' does the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This red-bracted plant, sold at Christmas, is grown for its showy leaves that look like blooms.
